question: is the image null encoder-general, or a USFM artefact? Test with PyRadiomics raw-pixel texture.

representation.note: metadata columns (ga_weeks, plane_conf, ids, dates) EXCLUDED — ga_weeks in particular would have injected the GA channel into the image block

ga_leakage.note: USFM PC1 carries GA at 0.276; radiomics spreads it to PC3 (0.263). Both encode maturation, differently distributed.

THE_TWO_ENCODERS_AGREE.reading: radiomics and USFM held-out canonical correlation is +0.963 — they are near-interchangeable views of the same images. Any null found on one is therefore expected on the other, which makes this a WEAK independence check: it tests encoder architecture, not information content.

CARDIAC_REPLICATES_BUT_DOES_NOT_LOCALISE.VERDICT: the cardiac block is the ONLY signal replicating on both representations and surviving BH (radiomics q=0.012, USFM q=0.080), and it is NOT echo image quality — adding quality to the covariates INCREASES it. But it does not localise: of 11 cardiac variables only Percentil_LV_basal exceeds 0.08 on both (radiomics 0.129, USFM 0.165), and the per-variable profiles agree only at r=0.663. A block-level 0.11-0.17 spread thinly across 11 variables with one weak anchor is not yet an interpretable finding.

CONCLUSION: Radiomics does NOT overturn the image null, and it sharpens one candidate. Maternal collapses on BMI in both (0.298->0.023, 0.512->0.003). Doppler is dead on radiomics (-0.021, p=0.648), which further undermines the cerebral->Doppler hit that already failed localisation. Growth replicates (measurement recovery). CARDIAC is the one thing that survives on both encoders, is not explained by image quality, and merits a targeted follow-up — but its per-variable profile is too diffuse to call a finding today.
caveats: radiomics<->USFM cc=0.963 means this is NOT an independent encoder check in the sense intended; both are frame-level summaries of the same pixels and agree almost completely
the earlier archived image<->cardiac claim (0.248) still does not reproduce; this is a different, much weaker cardiac signal on the percentile-scored panel columns
